title: Corporate Travel Programmes: Measurement and Charging of Transaction Overage
content:
Booking transactions are counted for each billing period against the tier's included allowance, and every transaction beyond it is charged at the tier's overage rate. This is how the Corporate Travel Programmes measure and price use of the platform beyond what the subscription carries.

## What is counted, and over what window

The window is the billing period, running from the period start date to the period end date carried by the subscription for that period. What is counted inside it is the booking transaction fees raised on the same programme.

The count is taken on transactions actually completed in the period, so a booking made in one period and cancelled in the next still counts in the period it was made.

Transactions on a suspended programme are not counted, because no booking may be made while it is suspended.

## The charge

The quantity charged is the transactions counted in the period less the tier's included allowance, taken as nil where the count does not exceed the allowance. The overage charge for the period is that quantity multiplied by the tier's rate for each transaction beyond the allowance.

Overage is charged once for the whole period rather than transaction by transaction, and is stated on the invoice with the count it was measured over.

An unused allowance is never carried into the next period and is never credited back.

## Where the allowance is exceeded repeatedly

Where a company exceeds its allowance in 3 consecutive periods it is offered the tier above, and the overage continues to be charged until the move takes effect.

## The charge worked through on hypothetical figures

Take a hypothetical company on the Business Team Programme, whose allowance is 50 booking transactions a month and whose rate beyond the allowance is 4.00 for each transaction.

| Transactions counted in the period | Quantity beyond the allowance | Overage charged for the period |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 38 | nil | nil |
| 50 | nil | nil |
| 51 | 1 | 4.00 |
| 74 | 24 | 96.00 |

The row at 50 shows the boundary: an allowance is exhausted, not exceeded, when the count equals it, and the first chargeable transaction is the one after. A period in which only 38 transactions were counted leaves 12 of the allowance unused, and those 12 are neither carried forward nor credited back.
